newsitem.title: DUBAI: Stronger bourses needed to lure home Gulf capital.
newsitem.headline: Stronger bourses needed to lure home Gulf capital.

text.p: Gulf Arab states must develop their fledgling capital markets to lure home hundreds of billions of dollars invested abroad by their citizens and boost their oil-driven economies, a leading economist said on Monday.

"Measures should be in place to attract Gulf-owned funds from abroad. It is a vast pool to tap, at least ten times the value of the GCC (Gulf Cooperation Council) market's capitalisation today," Arab Banking Corp chief economist Paul Papadopoulos told the annual Emirates International Forum.
Experts have estimated Gulf citizens have between $600 billion and $800 billion invested overseas.
Papadopoulos said Gulf states needed to accelerate efforts to develop capital markets.
"The Gulf capital markets have far to go. Their total capitalisation is barely $70 billion," he said. "Capitalisation of Turkey's Istanbul market alone is nearly $19 billion."

Some Gulf Arab states have moved to cross list shares on their bourses. But Saudi Arabia, the region's dominant political and economic power, has said it had no immediate plans to link its bourse with other regional stock markets.
Most Gulf Arab stock markets are dominated by financial stocks, which represent over 50 percent of total GCC market capitalisation, said Papadopoulos.
He said certain steps needed to be taken to develop the role of Gulf capital markets in the region's economies.
These included linking bourses and encouraging expatriate residents, which make up a large share of the region's workforce, to invest their savings in the Gulf.

"The development of a sound Gulf-wide capital market operated by professionals is a necessary condition...for the establishment and growth, both in breadth and depth, of fixed capital formation," he said.
The GCC is an economic and political alliance composed of Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, United Arab Emirates, Bahrain, Qatar and Oman.
